topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiological factors and epidemiological evidence in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic biological processes, environmental exposures, and chance in driving cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens as drivers of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how microbial and viral infections contribute to oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and promotional carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms, metabolic activations, and cellular contexts by which mutagens, radiation, and non-mutagenic promoters induce cancer.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their effects.

topics.label: Concluding remarks on carcinogen exposure and risk assessment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within personal and societal risk-benefit assessments.
